items.name: 2 Handed Kettlebell Swing
items.description: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell with both hands in front of you. Hinge at the hips to swing the weight back between your legs, keeping your back flat and knees slightly bent. Drive your hips forward explosively to swing the weight up to chest height, letting the momentum carry it. It primarily works the hamstrings and glutes, with the quads and abs assisting as secondary movers. Let the weight swing back down naturally as you hinge into the next repetition, keeping the movement continuous.

items.name: Seated Hip Adduction
items.description: Sit or lie using the machine or a resistance band, positioning the pads or band against the outside of your legs. Squeeze your legs together against the resistance, focusing on your inner thighs. Pause briefly at the end of the range, then return to the starting position with control. It primarily targets the glutes. Keep the movement slow and controlled rather than using momentum.

items.name: Arnold Shoulder Press
items.description: Using a pair of dumbbells, bring the weight to shoulder height with your hands set slightly wider than shoulder width. Press the weight upward and slightly inward until your arms are fully, but not aggressively, extended overhead. Pause briefly at the top, then lower back down under control to the starting position at shoulder level. It primarily works the shoulders, with the trapezius and triceps assisting as secondary movers. Keep your core braced and avoid arching your lower back excessively as you press.

items.name: Axe Hold
items.description: Get into position with your body forming a straight line from head to heels, supported on your forearms or hands and feet. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips from sagging or piking upward. Hold the position for the desired time while breathing steadily and keeping your neck in a neutral position. Stop before your form breaks down to avoid unnecessary strain on your lower back.

items.name: Barbell Ab Rollout
items.description: Kneel on the floor holding a barbell in front of you with both hands. Slowly roll the wheel or bar forward, extending your body out as far as you can while keeping your core braced. Stop before your lower back begins to sag, then reverse the movement by pulling back to the starting position using your abs. It primarily targets the obliquus externus abdominis. Keep the movement slow and controlled throughout, avoiding any arching in your lower back.

items.name: Barbell Hack Squats
items.description: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell positioned securely across your upper back or at chest height. Bend at the hips and knees to lower your body, keeping your chest up and your knees tracking in line with your toes. Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive back up through your heels to standing. It primarily works the quads, with the hamstrings and glutes assisting as secondary movers. Keep your core braced and your back neutral throughout the movement to protect your spine.

items.name: Barbell Lunges Standing
items.description: Stand tall holding a barbell, then step forward into a long stride, stepping forward and returning to the start each rep. Lower your body until both knees are bent to roughly 90 degrees, with your front knee tracking over your ankle. Push through your front heel to return to the starting position, then repeat on the other leg. It primarily works the quads, with the glutes assisting as secondary movers. Keep your torso upright and your core engaged to maintain balance throughout.

items.name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
items.description: Sit with your forearms resting on your thighs or a bench, holding a barbell and a bench with an overhand grip. Let the weight roll down toward your fingertips, allowing your wrists to extend. Curl the weight back up by flexing your wrists as far as comfortable, then lower with control. Use a light weight and move slowly, since the wrist is a small, easily strained joint.

items.name: Barbell Triceps Extension
items.description: Hold a barbell overhead or at chest height, keeping your upper arm close to your head or torso. Extend your arm at the elbow until it is fully straight, keeping your upper arm still. Slowly bend your elbow to return to the starting position, controlling the weight on the way down. It primarily works the triceps, with the shoulders and chest assisting as secondary movers. Keep your elbows tucked in and avoid flaring them out to the sides.

items.name: Barbell Wrist Curl
items.description: Sit with your forearms resting on your thighs or a bench, holding a barbell and a bench with an underhand grip. Let the weight roll down toward your fingertips, allowing your wrists to extend. Curl the weight back up by flexing your wrists as far as comfortable, then lower with control. It engages the biceps as supporting muscles. Use a light weight and move slowly, since the wrist is a small, easily strained joint.

items.name: Abdominal Stabilization
items.description: Using a gym mat, lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, hands lightly supporting your head. Curl your shoulders up and forward off the floor by contracting your abs, without pulling on your neck. Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then lower back down with control. It primarily works the abs, with the obliquus externus abdominis assisting as secondary movers. Keep the movement slow and controlled, focusing on squeezing your abs rather than momentum.

items.name: Bear Walk 2
items.description: Pick up a heavy weight in each hand and stand tall with your shoulders back and your core braced. Walk forward with controlled, steady steps, keeping the weight from swinging side to side. Maintain an upright posture throughout the distance or time, breathing steadily as you move. It primarily works the shoulders, calves, chest, abs, and other supporting muscles, with the glutes, lats, obliquus externus abdominis, quads, and other supporting muscles assisting as secondary movers. Set the weight down with control at the end of the set rather than dropping it.

items.name: Single Leg Extension
items.description: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and the ankle pads resting just above your feet. Extend your legs upward until they are straight, squeezing your quads at the top of the movement. Lower the weight back down slowly and under control until your knees return to roughly 90 degrees. It primarily targets the quads. Avoid locking your knees out aggressively at the top of each repetition.

items.name: Bench Press
items.description: Lie on a flat bench and take a grip slightly wider than shoulder width on the bar or dumbbells, positioning it directly above your chest. Lower the weight with control to your chest, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso. Press the weight back up powerfully until your arms are fully extended, without locking out aggressively. It primarily works the chest, with the shoulders and triceps assisting as secondary movers. Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down, and your feet flat on the floor for a stable base.

items.name: Benchpress Dumbbells
items.description: Lie on a flat bench and take a grip slightly wider than shoulder width on the bar or dumbbells, positioning it directly above your chest. Press the weight back up powerfully until your arms are fully extended, without locking out aggressively. It primarily works the chest, with the shoulders and triceps assisting as secondary movers. items.name: Bench Press Narrow Grip
items.description: Lie on a flat bench and take a narrow grip on the bar or dumbbells, positioning it directly above your chest. Lower the weight with control to your chest, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso. Press the weight back up powerfully until your arms are fully extended, without locking out aggressively. It primarily works the triceps, with the shoulders and chest assisting as secondary movers. Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down, and your feet flat on the floor for a stable base.

items.name: Bent High Pulls
items.description: Set up with a pair of dumbbells, hinging at the hips with a flat back and a slight bend in your knees. Pull the weight toward your torso by driving your elbows back, leading with your elbows rather than your hands. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, then lower the weight back down under control. It primarily targets the trapezius. Keep your core engaged and avoid using your lower back to jerk the weight upward.

items.name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rows
items.description: Set up with a bench and a pair of dumbbells, hinging at the hips with a flat back and a slight bend in your knees. Pull the weight toward your torso by driving your elbows back, leading with your elbows rather than your hands. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, then lower the weight back down under control. It primarily targets the lats. Keep your core engaged and avoid using your lower back to jerk the weight upward.

items.name: Bent-over Lateral Raises
items.description: Stand holding a bench and a pair of dumbbells with a slight bend in your elbows, arms relaxed by your sides. Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach roughly shoulder height, leading with your elbows rather than your hands. Pause briefly at the top, then lower the weight back down slowly and under control. Use a light to moderate weight and avoid swinging your body to generate momentum.

items.name: Bent Over Rowing

items.description: Start using a barbell, arms extended by your sides with a grip that fits your setup and elbows tucked close to your torso. Squeeze at the top of the movement, then slowly lower back to the starting position under control. It primarily works the biceps, with the brachialis assisting as secondary movers. Keep your wrists neutral and your core braced throughout the set.

items.name: Body-Ups
items.description: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width and your body in a straight line. Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso. Press back up through your hands until your arms are fully extended, without letting your hips sag. It primarily works the triceps, with the shoulders and abs assisting as secondary movers. Keep your core braced throughout to maintain a straight line from head to heels.

items.name: Braced Squat
items.description: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your torso upright and your arms out in front of you or by your sides for balance. Bend at the hips and knees to lower your body, keeping your chest up and your knees tracking in line with your toes. Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive back up through your heels to standing. It primarily works the quads, with the glutes assisting as secondary movers. Keep your core braced and your back neutral throughout the movement to protect your spine.

items.name: Chest Press
items.description: Using light resistance or just your bodyweight, whichever the variation calls for, bring the weight to shoulder height with your hands set slightly wider than shoulder width. Press the weight upward and slightly inward until your arms are fully, but not aggressively, extended overhead. Pause briefly at the top, then lower back down under control to the starting position at shoulder level. It primarily targets the chest. Keep your core braced and avoid arching your lower back excessively as you press.

items.name: Burpees
items.description: Start standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent. Explosively jump upward or forward, driving through your legs and swinging your arms for momentum. Land softly with bent knees to absorb the impact before resetting for the next repetition. Focus on quality, controlled landings rather than maximum speed to reduce joint strain.

items.name: Butterfly
items.description: Lie back on a bench holding a pair of dumbbells above your chest with a slight bend in your elbows. Lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest. Bring your arms back together above your chest in the same arcing path, squeezing your chest at the top. It primarily works the chest, with the shoulders assisting as secondary movers. Keep the bend in your elbows fixed throughout to protect your shoulder joints.

items.name: Cable External Rotation
items.description: Sit or stand with your core engaged holding a cable machine, feet planted firmly on the floor. Rotate your torso to one side in a controlled motion, keeping your hips as stable as possible. Return to the center and rotate to the opposite side, alternating sides for the set. It primarily targets the shoulders. Move slowly and with control rather than twisting quickly, to protect your lower back.

items.name: Cable Woodchoppers
items.description: Sit or stand with your core engaged holding a cable machine, feet planted firmly on the floor. Rotate your torso to one side in a controlled motion, keeping your hips as stable as possible. Return to the center and rotate to the opposite side, alternating sides for the set. It primarily targets the obliquus externus abdominis. Move slowly and with control rather than twisting quickly, to protect your lower back.

items.name: Calf Press Using Leg Press Machine
items.description: Sit in the leg press machine with your feet placed shoulder-width apart on the platform, working both feet together. Release the safety catches and lower the platform by bending your knees toward your chest, keeping your lower back flat against the pad. Press the platform away by extending your legs, without locking your knees out completely at the top. It primarily targets the calves and soleus. Keep the movement controlled in both directions rather than bouncing at the bottom.

items.name: Calf Raises on Hackenschmitt Machine
items.description: Stand on the balls of your feet holding a machine, working both feet together, with your heels hanging off a step or platform if available. Rise up onto your toes as high as possible, squeezing your calves at the top of the movement. Lower your heels back down slowly, allowing a deep stretch at the bottom before the next repetition. It primarily works the calves, with the soleus assisting as secondary movers. Keep your legs straight but not locked, and control the tempo throughout.

items.name: Chin Up
items.description: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width and your arms fully extended. Pull your body upward by driving your elbows down and back until your chin clears the bar. Pause briefly at the top, then lower yourself back down with control to a full hang. It primarily works the biceps and lats, with the brachialis and trapezius assisting as secondary movers. Avoid leaning back excessively or using momentum to move the weight.

items.name: Close-grip Lat Pull Down
items.description: Sit at the machine and grip the bar with a close grip, then set your thighs securely under the pads. Pull the bar down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back, leading with your shoulder blades. Pause briefly, then let the bar rise back up under control until your arms are fully extended. It primarily targets the lats. Avoid leaning back excessively or using momentum to move the weight.

items.name: Cross-Bench Dumbbell Pullovers
items.description: Lie on a bench holding a pair of dumbbells with both hands above your chest, arms slightly bent. Lower the weight backward in an arc over your head until you feel a stretch through your lats and chest. Pull the weight back up along the same arc to the starting position above your chest, driven by your lats. It primarily targets the lats, chest, and serratus anterior. Keep your hips level and your core braced to avoid arching your lower back.

Gradually increase your pace or resistance to your target intensity, keeping your posture upright and relaxed. Maintain a steady rhythm and breathing pattern for the planned duration or distance. It primarily works the abs, with the obliquus externus abdominis assisting as secondary movers. Cool down at an easy pace for a few minutes at the end before stopping.

items.name: Deadbug
items.description: Get into the starting position on your hands and knees, or lying on your back, keeping your spine in a neutral, stable position. Slowly move the indicated limbs through the movement while keeping your core braced and your torso still. Move with control, avoiding any rocking or twisting of your hips and lower back. It primarily works the abs, with the obliquus externus abdominis assisting as secondary movers. Focus on quality over speed, since the goal is core control rather than momentum.

items.name: Deadhang
items.description: This is an advanced bodyweight hold that requires significant strength and body control to perform safely. Set up in the required position, bracing your core and shoulders to support your full bodyweight. Hold the position for the desired time, keeping your body tight rather than sagging or shaking excessively. Build up to this movement gradually with progressions before attempting the full version.

items.name: Deadlifts
items.description: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a barbell positioned over the middle of your feet. Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the bar, keeping your back flat and your chest lifted. Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees together to stand up straight, keeping the bar close to your body. Lower the weight back down with control by reversing the movement, hinging at the hips first. It primarily works the lats, with the glutes assisting as secondary movers.

Pause briefly, then let the bar rise back up under control until your arms are fully extended. It primarily works the lats, with the biceps and trapezius assisting as secondary movers. It primarily targets the calves. Keep your legs straight but not locked, and control the tempo throughout.

items.name: Wall Handstand

Set up in the required position, bracing your core and shoulders to support your full bodyweight. items.name: Wall Pushup
items.description: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width and your body in a straight line. Press back up through your hands until your arms are fully extended, without letting your hips sag. It primarily works the shoulders, chest, and triceps, with the glutes, abs, serratus anterior, and trapezius assisting as secondary movers. Keep your core braced throughout to maintain a straight line from head to heels.

items.name: Wall Squat

Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive back up through your heels to standing. It primarily targets the hamstrings and quads. Keep your core braced and your back neutral throughout the movement to protect your spine.

It primarily works the chest, with the shoulders, biceps, and triceps assisting as secondary movers. Keep your core braced and avoid arching your lower back excessively as you press.

Keep your core braced and avoid arching your lower back excessively as you press.

items.name: Pull-Ups (Wide Grip)
